result.title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs
result.summary: Attention in large language models (LLMs) scores every query against every key with a full dot product. We investigate whether this dot product must be computed completely for attention to be effective. We propose Hidden Sparse Attention (HiSA), which keeps the query and key projections intact but only computes a partial dot product, following a static, parameter-free rule set by the token positions: attention becomes sparse in the hidden (feature) dimension, an axis much less explored than token sparsity, rather than over tokens as in almost all sparse attention methods. Based on the structure of rotary position embeddings (RoPE), we decompose keys and queries into parts which can be omitted when computing attention. By training LLMs from scratch with HiSA, we find that this partial dot product does not hurt but improves performance compared with the complete product while computing only about a third of the query-key products. During inference HiSA improves decoding speed and shrinks memory footprint. We also extend HiSA to FlashAttention-3 kernels for training and inference. Finally, we motivate our approach by showing that dense attention learns to suppress the attention score parts that HiSA drops. Code is available at https://github.com/ambroise-b/hisa.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HiSA：保留 query/key 投影完整，但依 RoPE 结构把 key/query 拆成若干部分，按 token 位置的静态无参数规则只计算部分点积，使注意力在隐藏特征维度上稀疏；从零训练 LLM 并以 FlashAttention-3 实现。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「按位置规则裁剪注意力分数分量」及「稠密注意力会主动压低被裁剪分量」的观察，可能可供核查注意力结构与位置因素如何影响内部状态保留及降低计算成本的线索。
